web_title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: “Conviction is not a substitute for a margin of safety.”
epigraph.author: Research Desk maxim

web_blocks.text: The strongest bull case starts with a customer problem, not a stock chart. Data centers, semiconductor plants and other critical loads need dependable power; utility interconnection can take time; Bloom has an installed fleet, a reported one-segment business, repeat customer relationships and a recent jump in product demand. FY2026 guidance now implies $4.4–$4.6 billion of revenue, while Q3 gross margin was 33.8% and operating income was positive. If the company industrializes a modular platform, sustains service quality and converts project demand into cash, a much larger business is plausible. The Bull case is not imaginary. It is a multi-year execution plan. [1][2][3][18][19][20][21]

The bear case is that the market has capitalized that plan too early. The FY2025 audited record still showed a net loss and only $57.2 million of CFO less PP&E purchases. First-nine-month 2026 cash after PP&E was $41.6 million before affiliate investment while contract assets and inventory expanded. Customer concentration, high project finance needs, installation guarantees, service obligations and a 2026 diluted weighted-share count above the recent basic count all qualify the reported earnings rebound. The model’s base-case value is $75.98 per diluted share, below both the $201.93 cutoff close and the $158.76–$163.60 monitor band. [1][2][3]

web_blocks.caption: Probability-weighted 10-year outcomes; analyst scenarios, not guidance [1][2][3]
web_blocks.takeaway: The weighted value is about 51.8% below the verified close. The Bull outcome is possible but receives only a 15% weight because sustained growth, margin expansion and post-capex cash conversion remain unproven.

web_blocks.text: The hinge claim is cash conversion at scale. If 2026 record revenue is followed by accepted installations, service contribution, falling working-capital intensity and cash after necessary capex, the bull path gains probability. If contract assets remain elevated, inventory outruns shipments, guarantees absorb gross profit or outside financing remains essential, growth can disappoint even while order announcements continue. You and I should therefore monitor delivered and accepted megawatts, product and installation margins, service renewals and costs, contract-asset billing, CFO less PP&E, customer concentration and diluted shares. The topline alone cannot settle the dispute. [1][2][3]

web_blocks.text: The evidence-led action is to exit the existing tactical-momentum position rather than average down. The same-session positions ledger records 7.2505 shares in Schwab and 16.276072 in Robinhood, 23.526572 shares total. At the Nov 12 close their market value was $4,750.72 against $5,999.98 cost basis, a $1,249.26 unrealized loss and 5.24% of the recorded portfolio net worth. Cost basis is not a reason to keep a position whose base value is below market and whose trend is below the major averages. The recommendation is advisory; it is not a broker order. Confirm current price, tax lots and executed holdings before acting. [34][42]

If the Schwab account has a subsequent unrecorded transaction, update the broker log before using the share instruction. [42]

web_blocks.intro: Because the verdict is REJECTED, the deterministic risk-unit table assigns zero new capital. The $158.76–$163.60 band is a monitor-only reference, not an order; the $150.34 invalidation level must be recalculated from a future authorized entry and fresh prices.

web_blocks.text: Why cash rather than the next attractive story? The active shortlist includes quality companies with their own valid theses, but sale proceeds are not required to be reinvested immediately. MSFT and AVPT remained in Stage 2 at the Nov 12 cutoff; LNG also retained a Stage 2 label, yet its one-week advance was already strong. Their current technical status does not transfer BE’s risk budget automatically, and the broad index remained in correction. The outside peers CMI, GEV and VRT all carried weaker Stage 4 classifications on that same ledger. This is a stock-specific dossier, not a portfolio audit; cash is the only destination that does not smuggle in a second unreviewed thesis. [34][35][36][37][43]

Re-entry trigger: do not add BE until a fresh close reclaims the 50-day average at $244.92 and the 200-day average at $223.35, then holds a support retest; also require a refreshed base value above the new entry zone.

The monitoring plan has observable gates. Revisit Bloom after the next filed results and customer updates, but separate contracted frameworks from installed capacity. Track operating and service gross margins, receivables and contract assets, inventory conversion, warranty costs, cash after PP&E and diluted shares. Reopen the market decision only after those measures and the chart improve together. For the shortlist, refresh entry bands and overlap at the portfolio level before deploying the sale proceeds; for outside candidates, complete independent business and valuation research. If neither group clears the gates, cash remains the deliberate destination. [1][2][3][33]

book_paragraphs: You and I have reached the point where a balanced story must become a decision. The bull case is straightforward: customers need power, some grid connections are delayed, and Bloom has a working product with a growing set of deployments. Revenue guidance is $4.4–$4.6 billion for 2026, Q3 gross margin was 33.8% and operating income was positive. If factory learning lowers cost and the installed fleet becomes a profitable service base, Bloom could become much more than a niche fuel-cell maker. We should acknowledge that possibility without treating it as a guaranteed result. [1][2][3][18][19][20][21]

Now steelman the bear. FY2025 ended with a GAAP net loss and only about $57 million of cash after PP&E purchases. The first nine months of 2026 showed just $41.6 million after PP&E before affiliate investment, even as contract assets and inventory grew. The company also carries significant debt-like obligations and customer concentration. This does not mean the business is failing; it means the high-growth narrative has not yet produced a mature cash engine. You should follow project acceptance and customer billing, not only bookings and announced megawatts. [1][2][3]

The DCF makes our disagreement measurable. Starting with $4.5 billion of 2026 guided revenue and a 1.36% nine-month cash-after-PP&E margin, the ten-year bear, base and bull cases yield approximately $13.50, $75.98 and $384.71 per diluted share. We weight them 40%, 45% and 15%, producing $97.30 expected value versus the Nov 12 close of $201.93. The bull can clear the quote, but it needs 30% revenue growth for a decade and an 18% terminal FCF margin. The base is already an ambitious 20% growth path. These are our scenarios, not management forecasts. [1][2][3]

The single hinge claim is whether revenue growth can become cash after the factory and working-capital needs are funded. If accepted installations grow, service contributions remain healthy, contract assets bill and collect, and CFO exceeds ongoing plant needs, Bloom earns more credibility. If installation losses, guarantees, customer concentration or financing needs persist, additional sales may add less equity value than the headline growth implies. Your scorecard should therefore connect installed megawatts to acceptance, service margin, cash conversion, customer concentration and diluted shares. [1][2][3]

Our horizon calls differ. Over weeks to six months, the tape and model do not justify new capital. Across six to twenty-four months, keep the business on a conditional watch and judge delivery against guidance. Across three to ten years, the platform may be meaningful, but the current price still requires durable growth and a much stronger cash margin. If the company proves that conversion, revisit the valuation. If it does not, a powerful need for electricity will not rescue every supplier that tries to meet it. [1][2][3]

The position ledger records 7.2505 Bloom shares at Schwab and 16.276072 at Robinhood. Together that is 23.526572 shares, marked at $4,750.72 at the Nov 12 close, versus $5,999.98 cost. The unrealized loss is $1,249.26 and the position is 5.24% of reported net worth. Those figures describe the recorded books, not an order or guaranteed execution price. The transaction file assumes the Schwab ledger is accurate through its Nov 10 last transaction; verify any later activity and tax lots before you act. [34][42]

My recommendation is to exit the full tactical-momentum position rather than add to it. The business is conditional, not a fundamental failure, but the DCF base lies below the support band and the Nov 12 close sits below both 50-day and 200-day averages. The decision follows price, cash conversion and expected value together; it is not a judgment that the technology has no future. If you believe the bull path is materially more likely, the right response is a fresh re-underwrite with explicit probabilities—not averaging down because the cost basis is higher. [1][2][3][34]

Where should the proceeds go? The shortlist shows MSFT and AVPT in Stage 2 on the Nov 12 ledger, and LNG also in Stage 2 after a strong one-week move. Those prior theses deserve a current portfolio-level refresh; this BE report does not certify them as substitute buys. Outside peers CMI, GEV and VRT are useful comparisons, yet each had a Stage 4 classification on the cutoff date. When the benchmark is in correction and no full second thesis has been refreshed here, cash is an active choice. It prevents one exit from becoming an automatic concentration in another name. [34][35][36][37][43]

Your next checklist is concrete. Revisit Bloom after filed results, accepted installations and cash-flow updates. Revisit the shortlist only after checking its current prices, entry bands, correlation and overlap with the rest of the account. Revisit outside names after a business and valuation review. If none clears the evidence and support-zone hurdles, do not force the proceeds into an equity. A patient cash balance can buy you the option to act when both the business and the market are again cooperating. [1][2][3][33]

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A good company can still be a poor purchase at a demanding price. Your action here is not a prediction that Bloom disappears; it is a decision that the base evidence does not justify this capital at this valuation and technical structure. Sell the tactical thesis, keep the proceeds liquid, and let the next evidence—not the old cost basis—set the next move.
